concepts.rpz2: A failure mode in which generated code is structurally valid, type- correct, syntactically well-formed, and superficially aligned with the specification, yet behaves divergently from specification intent. The dominant failure mode of agentic coding above the complexity threshold (O-41). Distinguished from hallucination (which produces non-existent references and typically fails at compile time) and syntax error (which fails parsing). Plausible-but-wrong realizations are valid syntactically, valid type-wise, and surface-plausible behaviorally; they survive unit testing because unit tests verify only the realizations the test author thought to enumerate.

The property of invariant-level interoperability between two semantic governance systems. Two governance systems are constitutionally compatible if they can interoperate without either system violating its own declared invariants in the process. This is compatibility at the constitutional layer — not protocol compatibility (message format agreement), not semantic compatibility (shared vocabulary), but structural compatibility (shared invariant space within which interoperation can occur without governance violation). Three named incompatibility types: (1) Invariant Conflict — the two systems hold directly contradictory invariants, such that any shared operation would violate at least one; (2) Scope Conflict — the two systems have overlapping jurisdictional claims over the same operations or artifacts, producing competing governance demands; (3) Authority Conflict — the two systems hold competing warrant claims over the same authority source, without a declared resolution mechanism. Where incompatibilities exist, constitutional compatibility can be achieved through explicit mapping layers that translate between governance regimes — these are termed compatibility bridges.

concepts.rpz2: The database-type instantiation of the Ableman Format Specification (AFS), peer to the document-type instantiation (CX:AES, O-20). A governed corpus database in which entries are content-addressed (SP-18), authority-bound (CG-05), lineage-tracked (SP-20), and admissibility-gated (CG-04). Operations: insert, query, refuse, amend, withdraw — each producing receipts (CG-02). Hosts content types including the Constitutional Encyclopedia (CE, O-50), the Constitutional Dictionary (CD, O-51), and custom domain corpora (CONDEX, governance precedent stores, domain-specific governed corpora). The substrate enforces five governance properties at substrate level rather than as application-layer overlay: lineage preservation, admissibility gating, refusal as first-class outcome, content-addressed identity, receipt production across all governance-consequential operations.

The specification methodology through which the Ableman framework is itself specified, governed, and transmitted. A CX:AES (Agent-Executable Specification) Codex has three constitutionally distinct layers: CX-S — domain physics: what must hold in every valid instance (invariants, inadmissible regions) CX-C — configuration: what was chosen from the possibility space and why (selections, rationale, blast radius) CX-I — realization: how to construct or instantiate the system given CX-S constraints and CX-C decisions

The SCI framework separates CX-S domain possibility and invariants, CX-C design selection and rationale, and CX-I executable construction procedure so what could be built, what was chosen, and how to build it do not collapse.
